by_quarantine_region.justification: Reflection floods do not stop at the scheduled minute. In the gaps between consecutive attack windows the traffic to the victim continues at flood rate: the 11:46-11:50 gap on day 2 alone holds 556,201 flows — 81.6% of every benign flow in the dataset — 99.8% of them touching the victim, at roughly 139,000 flows/min against a genuine benign baseline near 70/min. But no window covers them, so the schedule cannot say which vector any one of those flows belongs to, and a flow that cannot be attributed to a class is not thereby benign. Across both days these gaps hold roughly 613,000 flows — about 90% of everything the closed-world assumption currently calls benign here. Calling that benign fabricates a class out of attack tail; calling it ddos invents an attribution the source does not support. Declining to answer is the only reading the evidence carries. The genuine benign baseline is not touched: the stretches before the first attack and after the last on each day stay adjudicated, and it is there (and in the ~65,600 flows with a measurable resp_bytes_per_pkt) that this dataset's real benign traffic lives. Evidence: docs/label_evidence.md B3. Arithmetic: each region runs from one window's end plus one minute — the end-of-minute extension labelling applies to every window — to the next window's start exactly, so the regions tile the gaps and touch neither neighbour.
